Corrected the fix in `src/dotenv/parser.py` only. The earlier version wrongly treated any value starting with `#` as a comment, breaking `KEY=#literal`.

Root cause: `_equal_sign` (`=[^\S\r\n]*`) consumes whitespace after `=`, so `KEY= # explanation` yields a value part beginning at `#` with no preceding whitespace for the `\s+#` strip to match.

Fix: `parse_binding` now captures the `_equal_sign` match and passes `len(equal_sign) > 1` (i.e. whitespace followed `=`) as `preceded_by_whitespace` through `parse_value` into `parse_unquoted_value`. Only when that flag is set AND the part starts with `#` does it return `""`.

Verified against all acceptance cases: `KEY=#literal`→`#literal`, `KEY=a#b`→`a#b`, `KEY=abc # note`→`abc`, `KEY= # explanation`→`""`, quoted `" # literal"`/`' # literal'`→` # literal`, `KEY=`→`""`. Quoting, exports, and ordinary comments are untouched.

Limitation: relies on `_equal_sign` being the sole consumer of post-`=` whitespace; if that regex changes, the `len > 1` heuristic must be revisited. Tests to be run by host.
